title: CSS comments and maintainable annotations
learningObjectives: Explain css comments and maintainable annotations and its role in modern CSS.
Write valid CSS syntax and predict the computed result.
Choose the technique appropriate to a real interface requirement.
Identify common implementation, accessibility, and browser-support pitfalls.
Test and explain the behaviour using browser developer tools.

understand.concept: CSS comments begin with /* and end with */. They can span multiple lines and are ignored by the CSS parser. Use comments to explain intent, constraints, browser workarounds, component boundaries, or unusual values—not to restate an obvious declaration. CSS does not support JavaScript-style // comments; using them can invalidate the remainder of a declaration block. Comments are visible in source files and developer tools, so never place credentials, personal data, or secrets in them.
understand.whyItMatters: Readable stylesheets help teams understand design decisions and safely change components. Incorrect comment syntax can silently disable rules and create confusing visual defects.
understand.analogy: A CSS comment is a margin note in a recipe: it helps the next cook understand why a step exists, but it is not an ingredient.
understand.analogyLimit: Comments do not enforce the rule they describe and can become misleading when the code changes.

explain.narrative: Identify valid block comments, a broken double-slash comment, and an obsolete note. Refactor comments so they explain intent and remove stale or sensitive information.

examples.code:
/* Component: alert banner. Keep text contrast high on every status colour. */
.alert{padding:1rem;border-inline-start:4px solid currentColor}
examples.explanation: A block comment documents the component's intent and accessibility constraint. The CSS declaration remains active after the closing comment marker.
examples.expectedOutput: A padded alert with a leading border using currentColor.

examples.explanation: CSS does not define // comments. A browser may treat the unexpected tokens as part of a declaration value and discard that declaration; remove the line or replace it with a block comment.
examples.expectedOutput: The card grid and gap apply; the border-radius declaration may be invalid because of the misplaced // tokens.

practise.guidedTask: Find invalid // comments and stale comments in a stylesheet. Replace them with accurate block comments and verify the computed styles in DevTools.
practise.independentTask: Write a short comment policy for a component library. Explain which decisions deserve comments and which should be expressed through names, tests, or documentation.
hints: Do not put secrets or private information in source comments.
Re-check comments whenever the related implementation changes.

questions.prompt: Which syntax starts a CSS comment?
questions.explanation: CSS comments use the block-comment delimiters /* and */.

questions.prompt: Can a CSS block comment span multiple lines?
questions.explanation: CSS block comments can contain line breaks.

questions.prompt: Does CSS define // as a line comment?
questions.explanation: The CSS comment syntax is /* ... */; // is not a CSS comment.

options: One that explains a non-obvious design constraint
One that repeats every property name
One that stores an API secret
questions.answer: One that explains a non-obvious design constraint
questions.explanation: Comments should explain intent or constraints that are not clear from the code.

questions.prompt: Should credentials be stored in CSS comments?
questions.explanation: Comments remain visible in source and must not contain secrets.
